newsitem.title: ITALY: Telecom Italia to fuse into Stet.
newsitem.headline: Telecom Italia to fuse into Stet.

text.p: Italian telephone operating company Telecom Italia will be incorporated into the state-controlled telecommunications holding company Stet, the Italian Treasury said in a statement on Friday.
The merger is a key step towards the privatisation of the state telecom industry, which is due later this year.
The Treasury, which took over control of Stet from state holding IRI at the start of the year, indicated that the newly merged company would take Telecom Italia's name.

Stet and Telecom Italia are expected to hold board meetings on January 30 to approve the merger and appoint advisors to evaluate the deal. Full terms of the merger are expected between the end of June and the end of August with the privatisation slated for the end of October.
Stet, which controls Telecom Italia along with cellular phone operator Telecom Italia Mobile, is the fourth largest telecoms company in the world in terms of revenue.

Italian media reported on Friday that the Treasury planned to replace Stet's current managing director, Ernesto Pascale, with Tommaso Tommasi di Vignano, who is currently director-general of Telecom Italia, before the sell-off.
